text:
The Rangers celebrated their hundredth anniversary on Monday with a pregame ceremony at the Garden and then a 3-1 win over Montreal, their third straight. They have outscored teams 11-3 in that run and taken 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), so the streak has substance. At 13-8-1 with 27 points, Mike Sullivan's team looks like what its numbers say it is.

Those numbers are good. New York has 53.98% of the expected goals this season, and our projection puts it around 96 points with a 71% playoff chance. The Rangers have scored 7.33 fewer goals than their chances deserved. The goaltending has covered for it, saving 5.35 more than expected.

The net is the busiest storyline in the building. Igor Shesterkin has a .926 save percentage and 4.0 goals saved above expected over his last four starts. Dylan Garand is at .930 and 3.8 above expected over his last five. Joonas Korpisalo is back from a long stint on injured reserve and stopped 24 of 25 against Montreal. James Reimer's comeback ended with his contract terminated earlier this month.

The forward group has found unlikely help: Glenn Gawdin scored his first two NHL goals against Vancouver, and Will Cuylle had two more on Monday. The line to watch is J.T. Miller, Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye, which has 64% of the expected goals but has been outscored 7-4. That gap between chances and goals is the thing to watch.
headline: A centennial team with too many goalies and too few goals
